## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	// The request implementer (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §16) — the engine's one built-in
2	// task, and the only one that may read an item's `Model`.
3	//
4	// A person marks an ordinary issue `task:origin:ad-hoc`; the scheduler run adopts
5	// it by writing the machine block onto that issue and applying the first status —
6	// the issue IS the item (§16.1); this task's precondition decides, at pickup,
7	// whether the run happens; the session implements the issue and leaves a pull
8	// request. There is no code-work phase at all: the authorization a worker would
9	// have performed is the precondition's, and the item's `Request:` field — which
10	// names the item's own issue — is the whole payload.
11	
12	// Push permission, as the permission API answers it. `triage` and `read` are
13	// deliberately not here: the ask was push access, and a read-only collaborator
14	// rides every webhook payload as `COLLABORATOR` (F30).
15	export const PUSH_PERMISSIONS = ['admin', 'maintain', 'write'];
16	
17	// Who, if anyone, with push access asked for this. Pure over the `request` signal's
18	// read, so the judgment is testable without GitHub and the reads stay where every
19	// other read is.
20	export function eligibility(req) {
21	  if (PUSH_PERMISSIONS.includes(req.authorPermission)) {
22	    return { ok: true, why: `opened by @${req.author}, who has push access` };
23	  }
24	  const blessed = (req.approvals ?? []).find((a) => PUSH_PERMISSIONS.includes(a.permission));
25	  if (blessed) return { ok: true, why: `approved by @${blessed.login} with \`/claude go\`` };
26	  return { ok: false, why: 'neither opened nor approved with `/claude go` by anyone with push access on this repository' };
27	}
28	
29	export default {
30	  // The literal, not the constant beside it in `built-in-tasks.mjs`: the
31	  // declaration-shape check reads this file statically and cannot resolve an
32	  // import. The two are pinned to each other in request-mode.test.mjs.
33	  id: 'implement-request',
34	  // MANUAL: the scheduler run never puts this on a calendar. An item exists only because an
35	  // issue was marked, which is what makes a request a first-class origin of work
36	  // rather than a schedule nobody asked for.
37	  frequency: 'manual',
38	  // The read the precondition judges on. It is collected for THIS item — the issue
39	  // its `Request:` field names — which is why the precondition takes the item.
40	  precondition_signals: ['request'],
41	  // The default when the asker named no family; the item's `Model:` overrides it,
42	  // and only because this task declares the field below.
43	  agent_model: 'opus',
44	  model_from_request: true,
45	  // The ceiling the executor enforces in code. It is `merged-pr` because ONE shape
46	  // of request may land its own change: an asker who applied `claude-automerge`
47	  // said up front that a NARROW diff needs no approval (§16.11), and the item
48	  // carries that as its `Merge:` field. A ceiling is a maximum, not an
49	  // instruction: with no such field the worker opens a pull request and parks at
50	  // the approval lane exactly as every request did before, and with one it still
51	  // parks whenever the diff classifier calls the diff wide.
52	  expected_outcome: 'merged-pr',
53	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
54	  agent_execution_timeout: 4 * 3600,
55	  // A run that died mid-flight leaves a branch, a PR, or neither, and only a person
56	  // can say whether the half-done work stands — so nothing re-queues it mechanically.
57	  on_interrupt: 'needs-human',
58	
59	  // THE SECURITY CHECK, and it happens where every verdict happens: once, at pickup,
60	  // on the executor (§6.4). Three refusals, each a plain no-go that converges the
61	  // item to the rejected terminal — a refusal is nobody's inbox, and an ad-hoc item
62	  // has no anchor to roll to. On a marked issue that terminal stands on the OPEN
63	  // issue: the run's verdict is not the issue's validity (§16.5).
64	  //
65	  // A READ FAILURE IS NOT A VERDICT (F27). The decline's write-back cannot reach an
66	  // issue it cannot read, so declining on a rate limit or a 500 would strand
67	  // `claude-queued` on the issue forever over nothing — the request silently eaten.
68	  // Only a definitive `gone` declines; anything else FAILS the run, which parks the
69	  // item open in the failure lane where the ordinary re-queue lever retries it.
70	  precondition(signals, config, item) {
71	    const req = signals.request;
72	    if (!req) {
73	      return { error: `this item names no readable request (its \`Request:\` field is ${item?.request ? `#${item.request}` : 'missing'})` };
74	    }
75	    if (req.unreadable) return { error: `issue #${req.number} could not be read: ${req.error} — refusing to guess` };
76	    if (req.gone) return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} does not exist` };
77	    if (req.state !== 'open') return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} was closed before this ran` };
78	    if (!req.queued) {
79	      return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} no longer carries the mark — the request was withdrawn` };
80	    }
81	    const verdict = eligibility(req);
82	    return verdict.ok
83	      // No `context`: adoption already bound this item to its issue, and a second
84	      // line saying the same thing renders as two near-identical bullets in the one
85	      // section the session is told to read as its scope (seen on the first live
86	      // request, #1074/#1075).
87	      ? { run: true, reason: `#${req.number}: ${verdict.why}` }
88	      : { run: false, reason: `#${req.number}: ${verdict.why}` };
89	  },

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
# logic. It carries no cron; the scheduler workflow's drain is the guaranteed
# delivery and a label event is latency sugar.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
          # Every declared task's `required_secrets`, plus the configured endpoint
          # tokens, regenerated by the wiring converge. Actions requires each secret
          # to be named statically, so this list is the whole delivery mechanism; a
          # worker then reads process.env.<NAME>.
          #
          # The converge writes the list directly beneath this line, so it stays last.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs

  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: failure() || cancelled()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Continue the drain, or escalate a chain that keeps dying
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_CONTINUATION_DEPTH: ${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor-continuation.mjs
